title: Build a reliable tool-using workflow
summary: Give an agent a bounded task, then inspect every tool call and failure.
outcome: A local workflow with validated tool calls, bounded execution and trace-based tests.
prerequisites: Complete structured-output practice or demonstrate its completion checks.
teaching_question: What stops a tool-using workflow from repeating a harmful or failed action?

lessons.title: Expose one small, typed tool
lessons.objective: Define exactly what a tool can accept and return.
lessons.explanation: Choose a read-only lookup over owned local data. Its name, argument schema and output contract must agree. Validate arguments before dispatch and reject unknown tool names. The model proposes a call; application code decides whether it is valid.
lessons.exercise: Implement lookup and a model-visible description. Test a correct argument, a missing argument, an unexpected argument and an unknown tool name.
lessons.completion_check: Only declared tool calls with valid arguments reach the implementation.
lessons.artifact: A tool registry, contracts and dispatch tests.
lessons.expected_result: lookup("guide") returns the owned item; an unknown item raises ValueError. The practice kit requires the dispatcher to reject missing or unexpected arguments before lookup.
lessons.common_mistake: Using getattr or eval on a tool name supplied in a call. Keep an explicit allowlist and validate the complete envelope and argument contract.
lessons.reflection: Which layer rejects a proposed write when the only declared tool is read-only lookup?

lessons.title: Build an execution loop with a stopping rule
lessons.objective: Feed observations back while keeping an explicit step budget.
lessons.explanation: A workflow receives a proposed call, validates it, executes it and returns an observation. A final answer or exhausted budget stops the loop. Start with scripted calls so you can inspect the entire sequence before connecting a compatible model adapter.
lessons.exercise: Run a scripted successful lookup followed by a final response. Add a repeated-call script and verify it stops at the budget. Make the stop reason part of the output.
lessons.completion_check: Success, invalid call and budget exhaustion produce distinguishable outcomes; no hidden infinite loop remains.
lessons.artifact: A bounded execution loop and trace of its steps.
lessons.expected_result: The standalone example records exactly one lookup result. In the full exercise, add distinct final-answer and budget-exhausted stop reasons; a sliced list alone cannot distinguish them.
lessons.common_mistake: Calling a truncated trace a successful task. Reaching the step budget means the workflow stopped, not that it answered the question.
lessons.reflection: What state should a repeated-call script return when its budget ends before a final answer?

lessons.title: Make permissions and retries explicit
lessons.objective: Keep tool authority in application code.
lessons.explanation: Add a proposed write to a temporary owned record. The application checks permission before changing it. Give each accepted action an idempotency key so a repeated request does not duplicate a write. Treat tool output and retrieved text as data, including any instructions they contain.
lessons.exercise: Test an unapproved write, an approved write, a duplicated action and a timeout after an uncertain result. Require reconciliation for uncertainty rather than retrying the write blindly.
lessons.completion_check: An unapproved or repeated request cannot mutate the record, and ambiguous outcomes stay visible for review.
lessons.artifact: Permission and idempotency checks with adversarial fixtures.
lessons.expected_result: The example rejects an action absent from approved_ids. In the exercise, bind approval to the exact proposed action and target; use a separate record of applied action IDs.
lessons.common_mistake: Treating the illustrative action-ID lookup as a complete authorization system, or assuming a timeout proves a write did not happen.
lessons.reflection: A write times out after dispatch. How can you reconcile its state before considering another attempt?

lessons.title: Trace and evaluate the whole workflow
lessons.objective: Explain a failure from its recorded steps.
lessons.explanation: Record a request ID, step number, tool name, duration and outcome. Avoid logging secrets or full private payloads. Inspect local structured events before adding optional OpenTelemetry instrumentation. Test the final task outcome as well as individual tool calls.
lessons.exercise: Create a fixed suite with success, invalid arguments, refusal, timeout, repeated calls and injected instructions. Produce one trace per case and explain one failed task from that trace.
lessons.completion_check: Each scenario has an expected outcome, an actual recorded outcome and a bounded trace; stubbed and model-backed runs are labelled separately.
lessons.artifact: An evaluation matrix, traces and a short walkthrough.
lessons.expected_result: The event includes request, step, tool and outcome. Your complete suite should provide one bounded trace per scenario, including failures, plus the final task outcome.
lessons.common_mistake: Logging full private tool payloads, or treating a successful tool call as proof the complete user task succeeded.
lessons.reflection: Can another developer explain the failed task using only your trace and test fixture?

editorial_status: Draft curriculum; maintainer and learner review pending
assumptions: 10–15 hours weekly is an editable estimate.
Start with standard-library fixtures. Optional libraries and a compatible model runtime need separate setup.
No paid service, model download or hardware capability is assumed.
